name: adv_junction_fluid_split_enthalpy
source:
// One inflow, two outflows on a raw connect node: P equal, sum mdot zero, and
// h EQUAL on every branch (a split must not weight).
Source SRC(fluid$ = Water, mdot = 3.0, P = 400000, T = 350)
Valve  VA(Cv = 0.01, rho = 980, u = 1, model$ = fixed)
Valve  VB(Cv = 0.02, rho = 980, u = 1, model$ = fixed)
Sink   SA()
Sink   SB()
connect(SRC.out, VA.in, VB.in)
connect(VA.out, SA.in)
connect(VB.out, SB.in)
SA.P    = 300000
SB.mdot = 1.0
ha = VA.out.h
hb = VB.out.h
h1 = SRC.out.h
ma = VA.out.mdot
mb = VB.out.mdot
pn = SRC.out.P

error.message: There are 34 equations and 33 variables. The problem is overspecified and cannot be solved. Redundant relation (no free variable left to determine): CONNECT src.out, va.in, vb.in: src$out.p = va$in.p. A common cause: the same physics stated twice — a boundary pinning a quantity a component already defines (a re-equated mixer pressure, a T-pinned wall state), or two property calls restating one relation.
